thread:
olivia_support: FYI - VestaPay (dedicated) reporting lots of 429s and tail latency spikes since ~03:40 UTC. They run long-context chat (~10-14k tokens). I can repro a throttle on our side. ticket: https://support.redwood/v/2981 :sadpanda:

devon_eng: Can you paste the top-level logs and any eviction metrics? Also did autoscale fire?

olivia_support: Logs excerpt below (sanitized). Evictions + detached errors spiked at 03:40.

```
[03:39:58] kvcache.evictions_total=4123 window=5m
[03:39:58] kvcache.kv_fragmentation_ratio=0.77
[03:39:58] kvcache.alloc_failures=58
[03:40:01] tenant=vesta shards=8 auth_ok=true
[03:40:05] request_id=abc123 tokens=12240 model=gptx-long
[03:40:06] serving: throttled by kvcache (evicting) -> 429 to client
```

alex_sre: That fragmentation ratio is high. Looks like slab fragmentation + lots of long KV entries from longctx. If alloc_failures >0, runtime falls back to throttling instead of spilling. Was dedicated autoscale configured to allow burst?

olivia_support: Autoscale policy for this pool is conservative: min_instances=4, max_instances=12, scale_up_step=1, cpu_threshold=0.8. The pool didn't scale past 6. No recent capacity changes.

brian_runtime: Two hypotheses: 1) long-context chat causes large per-request KV slots that increase working set and fragment heap; 2) noisy tenant created many short-lived large KV windows -> fragmentation. We should check per-tenant kv object size distribution.

priya_cs: Customer complaining about retries and billing - they saw a billing bump because our client retries on 429. Can we confirm exact retry behavior in our SDK? They want credits if it's platform throttle.

devon_eng: Repro steps I used: single-stream curl loop sending 12k tokens prompt every 250ms to the same conversation id to heat KV. 

curl -X POST https://api.redwood/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \
  -d '{"model":"gptx-long","conversation_id":"repro-123","input":"<10k tokens>"}'

I get 429 / latency > 2s after ~120 reqs.

alex_sre: Quick mitigation options: 1) bump pool to max_instances=14 for this tenant (fast), 2) enable aggressive KV compaction (risk: CPU), 3) temporary tenant QoS throttle to cap per-tenant concurrent longctx sessions. Which do we want?

olivia_support: Customer asks for quickest fix — they need reduced 429s. Prefer scale bump + tenant QoS cap. Can ops do scale bump while eng prepares compaction patch?

brian_runtime: I'll push a runtime flag to trigger more aggressive slab compaction on the nodes hosting their shards. Patch is small but needs rollout. Will also add diagnostic metric: kvcache.per_tenant_avg_kv_size and kvcache.per_tenant_active_windows.

infra-bot: deploy request created #deploys/4739 - scale pool vesta-dedicated from 6 -> 14. ETA 5m.

priya_cs: Noted. I'll open a billing escalation and offer temporary credits pending root cause.

devon_eng: After scale bump, monitored for 10m: evictions dropped ~60%, 429s almost gone, fragmentation ratio slowly decreasing. Still seeing alloc_failures but at low rate.

alex_sre: Follow-ups: (a) reproduce in staging with a noisy tenant that simulates many longctx windows to validate compaction; (b) add fallback behavior: when alloc_failures > threshold, prefer spilling to disk-backed cache instead of immediate throttling; (c) update autoscale policy to consider kvcache.evictions in scale metric.

olivia_support: Great. I'll update ticket with timeline + actions. Thanks all :thumbsup:
